defect: market_stage4._tag derived the random-stream label from Python's built-in hash(str(...)). CPython randomises string hashing per process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is set; it is set nowhere in this repository and nowhere in the run environment (checked). Three separate interpreters produced three different labels for the same coordinates, so every run of stage 4 drew a DIFFERENT random stream. Results were internally consistent inside one process -- which is why the time-boundary check still passed -- but they did not reproduce across runs, and the docstring calling the tag 'stable' was wrong.
fix: the label is now blake2b(coordinates, digest_size=4), deterministic across processes, Python versions and platforms. Nothing else changed: the grid, the objective, the window rules, the budget, the selection rule and every metric are exactly as before.
verification: two fresh interpreters now produce an identical label and identical simulated values; the check runs inside run_market_stage4 and fails the run if it does not hold.
rerun: one re-run at the original grid, metrics and budget. The pre-fix artefacts are preserved unchanged under outputs/market/stage4_prehashfix/.

what_did_not_move.reading: every headline conclusion survives: 2020 is the only year all four cells favour re-estimating, 2022 is by far the worst, the four-year average is positive, and removing 2022 leaves it at roughly zero. Both sign flips are on cells whose difference is small enough to be inside or near the Monte-Carlo error, so they are not a change of finding.
